messages:
Ava (Product): Quick design review request — Private Setup wizard, network step. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz (please open). Main asks: tighten preflight UX, reduce error-recovery friction, polish copy for non-network folks, and fix a11y nits. PTAL before EOD.

Diego (Design): Skimmed it — overall good. Two quick things: stepper feels like a long form, and the 'network prerequisites' are scary for non-ops users. Suggest collapse by default and show a short ‘We will check’ summary. Also pushed a small copy idea: "Confirm connectivity from your management host to Redwood (TCP 443)" instead of generic 'open ports'.

Priya (Eng): Implementation note: we can run an automated preflight from a small agent run by the customer, or provide a script they run locally and upload results. The agent is nicer but some customers won't allow inbound. We have a prototype scanner: 
```
./tools/network-check --endpoint api.redwood-inference.com --ports 443,4430,5000
```
We can output JSON results suitable for upload.

Noah (Security): Small copy nit: avoid phrasing like 'open port 22' in docs — customers interpret that as inbound SSH. We should emphasize outbound egress to our control plane. Proposed microcopy: "Ensure outbound egress from your management host to control-plane hostnames (TCP 443). No inbound changes required by default." Also add a short sentence about KMS/HSM where relevant.

Sam (UX Research): Accessibility nits from quick pass: 1) Stepper doesn't set aria-current on the active step. 2) Error dialog traps focus but focus isn't returned to triggering element on close. 3) The orange warning color is ~3.8:1 — needs to meet 4.5:1 for AA contrast. Also keyboard users need a visible focus ring on the 'Upload result' button.

Diego (Design): Agree with Noah/Sam. For copy structure, can we do three levels: a one-line summary, a short expanded explanation, and a 'how to' with commands? Example: 
- One-liner: "We’ll verify your network can reach Redwood services (about 20s)."
- Expanded: "What we check: control plane reachability (TCP 443), DNS for *.redwood-inference.com, outbound NAT mapping."
- How-to: include copyable commands and an 'Upload result' option.

Ava (Product): The 3-tier copy sounds great. Product asks for: copyable commands, a toggle for 'Run checks from host' vs 'Upload preflight result', and an estimated time per check (e.g., ~20s). Also we should surface exactly what we test when something fails to reduce support tickets.

Priya (Eng): Copy button is trivial. For upload flow we'll accept a JSON file with a small schema — I'll attach schema later. Agent approach (agent -> control plane) needs a small allowance in design for telemetry opt-in. Progress spinner per-check is doable.

Noah (Security): One more legal/compliance ask: add a checkbox that records customer acknowledgment if they must change egress rules: "I understand this may require outbound network changes; I accept responsibility for these changes" — log this to audit events.

Sam (UX Research): VoiceOver wording: after success say "Network prerequisites complete" instead of just "Done" so it's explicit. Also when a step fails, expose the error code and a short remediation action first, then advanced logs behind a disclosure.

Diego (Design): Visual suggestion: inline status row per check with icon, verb, short detail, and a tooltip. Consistent verbs: 'Checking…', 'Verified', 'Action required'. Use accessible color/shape combos (check icon + green, spinner + amber, x + red). Add a keyboard-accessible 'Retry' action.

Zoe (Support): Add an FAQ note for customers behind strict egress NATs: "If your environment uses ephemeral outbound IPs, you can either use the upload flow or contact support for a static-eip option." That should cut down on tickets asking 'why did my check fail behind NAT'.

Ava (Product): Great. Diego — can you push the updated frames (collapsed prereqs, 3-tier copy, status rows, a11y fixes) by 16:00? @Priya please estimate dev hours for both agent and upload-only flows. @Sam can you run a quick keyboard + screen reader check once Diego updates? I'll collect final copy and lock for sprint.

Priya (Eng): Estimates: agent + UI + telemetry opt-in = 2 engs * ~5-7 workdays. Upload-only quick path (parse JSON + basic UI) = ~2 workdays.

Diego (Design): On it — updated Figma now includes the collapsed prereqs and an accessibility checklist. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz (updated). I also added inline copy examples: 
```
What we check
- Control plane reachability: TCP 443 to api.redwood-inference.com
- DNS resolution for *.redwood-inference.com
- Outbound NAT mapping: ensure response IPs are routable

How to run (copyable):
curl -sS https://api.redwood-inference.com/preflight | jq .
```

Sam (UX Research): I can run quick checks tomorrow AM (keyboard, NVDA, VoiceOver) and post notes. Prioritize focus management and aria-current.

Ava (Product): Thanks team — tagging for next sprint planning and support docs. I’ll compile the copy and accessibility checklist into a single spec.

Zoe (Support): Will draft an FAQ snippet and paste into the doc once copy is final.

Ava (Product): Closing loop — will follow up with PRD + acceptance criteria. Thanks :tada:
